helpText:
HelpThis ScreenKeywords (107)
SEO keywords from Google Keyword Planner, organized for content planning.

Quick Filters
One-click presets for common keyword analysis tasks:

  🎯 Quick Wins — Low competition + High intent keywords in Tier 1-2. Your easiest path to conversions. Start here.
  📈 Traffic Drivers — High-volume Tier 2 keywords (1,000+ searches/mo). Build authority and brand awareness.
  💰 Money Keywords — All high-intent keywords in Tier 1-2, regardless of competition. Your full conversion universe.
  🇫🇷 France Priority — French market Tier 1-2 keywords. Focus on your home market advantage.
  ✍️ Blog Ideas — Medium intent, low-medium competition keywords. Perfect for content calendar planning.
  ✕ Clear — Reset all filters to default.

Click any preset to instantly apply its filters. The preset deactivates if you manually change any filter.

Filtering
Use the dropdowns above each column to filter:

  Search — Type to find specific keywords
  Cluster — Content category (Gift Retirement, VHS Legacy, etc.)
  Market — 🇫🇷 France or 🇺🇸 US
  Tier — Relevance to MEMOPYK service
  Searches/mo — Monthly search volume ranges
  Comp. — How hard to rank (Low/Medium/High)
  Intent — Buyer readiness

Each filter supports multi-select: check/uncheck individual options, use Select All to toggle all. Click OK to apply, Cancel to revert.

Table Columns

  Keyword — The search term. Cluster shown inline as a 🏷️ Gift Retirement tag
  Market — 🇫🇷 FR = France, 🇺🇸 US = United States
  Tier — How relevant to MEMOPYK:
    
      Tier 1 = Direct service match (best!)
      Tier 2 = High relevance
      Tier 3 = Secondary
    
  
  Searches/mo — Monthly search volume from Google
  Competition — How hard to rank:
    
      Low = Easy to rank (good!)
      Medium = Moderate effort
      High = Hard to rank
    
  
  Intent — Conversion likelihood:
    
      High = Ready to buy (best!)
      Medium = Comparing options
      Low = Just researching
    
  
  Planned Posts — Number of planned posts targeting this keyword. Click to view in the Planned Posts tab.
  Posts — Number of published posts using this keyword. Click to view in the Posts tab.


Actions

  ✏️ Edit — Modify keyword details
  🗑️ Delete — Remove (with confirmation)


Best Strategy

  Start with Quick Wins preset — these are your best ROI keywords
  Use Traffic Drivers for brand awareness content
  Create planned posts targeting these keywords first
  Track progress via the Planned Posts and Posts counts

HelpThis Screen
  Planned Posts — Your Blog Article Backlog

  Each planned post is a blueprint for one blog article. It includes SEO keywords, target word count, content angle, suggested images, and internal linking opportunities. Think of this as your "what to write next" list.

  View Modes
  Toggle between two views using the buttons in the top-right corner:
  
    List — All posts in a flat list, sorted by status priority (In Progress → Planned → Backlog → Published).
    Grouped — Posts organized by topic cluster (e.g., "Photo Organization", "Video Memory"). Pillars appear first, followed by supporting articles.
  

  Stats Cards
  Four cards at the top show your content pipeline health:
  
    Total Topics — All planned posts in the system.
    Ready to Write — Posts with "backlog" status (research complete, ready to draft).
    In Progress — Posts actively being worked on or scheduled for publication.
    Posts Published — Completed articles published on memopyk.com.
  

  Filters
  Use the filter panel to narrow down posts:
  
    Search bar — Type keywords, post titles, or phrases to find specific topics.
    Article Role dropdown — Filter by pillar (main guides) or supporting articles.
    Topic Group dropdown — Show only posts from a specific cluster (25 clusters available).
    Category — Filter by MEMOPYK content category (Photo Organization, Video Memory, etc.).
    Status — Show only Backlog, Planned, In Progress, or Published posts.
    Type — Filter by content type (How-To, Storytelling Techniques, Holiday-Specific, etc.).
    Priority — Show only P1-P5 priority posts.
    Market buttons — All / 🇫🇷 France / 🇺🇸 English — filter by target market.
    Clear All — Reset all filters to default.
  

  Post Actions
  Click any post row to expand full details. Inside each expanded post:
  
    Edit — Modify the planned post metadata (keywords, word count, content angle, etc.).
    Delete — Remove this planned post (confirmation required).
    Create Post (orange button) — Turn this planned post into a blog post draft. Opens the post creation modal with all metadata pre-filled.
    View Posts — If this topic has been generated before, click to jump to the Posts tab filtered to show all posts created from this topic.
  

  Creating New Planned Posts
  Click Plan New Post (top right, orange button) to open the creation modal. Fill in:
  
    Title, primary keyword, secondary keywords
    Target word count, search volume, competition level
    Content angle (unique perspective for this article)
    Hero image concept, body image concepts
    Internal link opportunities (which MEMOPYK pages/services to link to)
    Category, type, priority, market (FR or EN)
    Article role (pillar or supporting), topic cluster
  

  Quick Tips
  
    Use Grouped view to see how many supporting articles you have per pillar.
    Filter by Priority P4-P5 to see high-value posts (high search volume, low competition).

helpText:
HelpThis Screen
  Image Bank — Centralized Media Library

  The Image Bank is your repository of royalty-free images for blog posts. Upload once, tag with labels, and reuse across multiple articles. The system automatically tracks where each image is used.

  Header Controls
  Two buttons in the top-right corner:
  
    Manage Labels — Open the label editor to create, rename, or delete colored labels for organizing images.
    Upload Images (orange button) — Add new images to the bank. Supports JPG, PNG, WebP up to 5MB each.
  

  Filters
  Three filter controls above the image grid:
  
    Category dropdown — Filter by content category (Photo Organization, Video Memory, Seasonal, etc.).
    Usage dropdown — Show all images, unused only, used in posts, hero images only, or body images only.
    Search bar — Search by filename, alt text, or image labels.
  

  Image Cards
  Each image card shows:
  
    Preview thumbnail — Hover to reveal action buttons (View, Edit, Delete).
    Usage badge (top-right) — Green "Used in N posts" or gray "Unused".
    Filename — Original filename when uploaded.
    Category badge — Content category (blue background).
    File size — Size in KB.
    Image labels — Colored label chips (up to 2 shown, +N more if additional labels exist).
  

  Image Actions
  Hover over any image card to reveal three action buttons:
  
    View (eye icon) — Open full image details: dimensions, file size, category, all labels, usage count, and list of posts using this image.
    Edit (pencil icon, orange) — Update alt text, category, or labels.
    Delete (trash icon, red) — Remove image from bank (confirmation required).
  

  Uploading Images
  Click Upload Images to open the upload modal:
  
    Drag and drop images or click the dropzone to browse files.
    For each selected image, add: alt text (optional), category, image labels (optional).
    Remove any file from the upload queue with the X button.
    Click Upload N Images to save to the bank.
  

  Managing Labels
  Click Manage Labels to open the label management modal:
  
    Type a new label name and click Create (orange button).
    Each label has a randomly assigned color (used in chips throughout the system).
    Click Edit (pencil icon) to rename a label.
    Click Delete (trash icon, red) to remove a label. If the label is used in N images, you'll be warned.
    Usage count shows how many images have this label.
  

  Quick Tips
  
    Use labels like "family", "technology", "seasonal-christmas", "hands" to organize images by subject.
    Filter by "Unused Only" to find images not yet used in any post (good candidates for new articles).
    The system automatically updates usage counts when you add/remove images from blog posts.
    Hero images and body images are tracked separately. Use the Usage filter to see which images are used as hero vs. body.
    Click any image to see which posts use it. Click a post link to jump directly to that post in the Blog Hub.

HelpThis ScreenBlog Editor
This screen lets you edit a blog post. All changes are saved only when you click Save Changes - nothing is saved automatically.

Top Bar
The top-right corner has action buttons:

  Discard (trash icon, red) - Only appears on blank drafts. Deletes the empty draft and returns to the Posts list. Use this if you created a post by mistake.
  AI Assist (sparkles icon) - Opens a dialog to generate content using AI. Fill in the topic, keywords, and notes, then click Generate. The AI uses Brand Brain context to write in MEMOPYK's voice. Takes 15-30 seconds. If the post already has content, you'll be asked to confirm before overwriting.
  Save Changes (orange) - Saves all fields at once: title, content, status, tags, hero image, and publication date
  Preview - Opens the published post in a new browser tab. Only available when the post status is Published
  Translation Assistant - Appears only for translation drafts (posts with "[TRANSLATE TO...]" in the title). Guides you through a 3-step translation process using your AI assistant, automatically preserving images.


AI Quick Start
When opening a blank draft, a purple Generate with AI banner appears in the content area. Click it to generate a full article instantly. You can also write manually - just start typing in the editor below the banner.

Fields (top to bottom)

Language - First field at the top. Choose French (fr-FR) or English (en-US). This determines which blog listing the post appears in and how AI generates content.

Title - The post headline. This is what readers see first.

Slug (URL) - The URL path for this post. Example: my-blog-post becomes /blog/my-blog-post. Use lowercase letters, numbers, and hyphens only.

Description (SEO) - A short summary shown in search engine results and social media previews. Keep it under 160 characters.

SEO Keywords
A green section for search optimization:

  Primary Keyword - The main search term this post targets
  Secondary Keywords - Additional related terms. Type and press Enter to add.


Hero Image
The main image displayed at the top of the post.

  Click Select Hero Image (or Change Hero Image if one is already set)
  A dialog opens with two options:
    
      Upload new image - Click Choose File to upload from your computer (PNG, JPG, GIF, WEBP, max 5 MB)
      Select from existing images - Click any image thumbnail to use it
    
  


Status & Publication Date
These two fields appear side by side.
Status - Choose the workflow stage:

  Draft - Work in progress, not visible to readers
  In Review - Ready for review before publishing
  Published - Live and visible on the blog
  Archived - Hidden from the public blog but preserved in the system


Published At - Controls when the post appears on the blog.

Tags

helpText: HelpThis ScreenCTA Button ManagementCTA stands for "Call to Action" — these are the main conversion buttons displayed across your website, designed to turn visitors into customers. MEMOPYK uses two CTA buttons: CALL (book a free consultation) and QUOTE (request a free quote). These buttons appear on every page and drive your key business actions.🎯 Why CTAs MatterYour CTA buttons are the primary way visitors take action on your site. CALL directs them to schedule a free consultation via your Cal.com booking page. QUOTE sends them to a Zoho Forms page to request a personalized quote. Keeping these buttons visible, well-labeled, and linked to the right destinations directly impacts your conversion rate.📋 Your CTA ButtonsTwo cards are displayed, one for each button. Each card shows:Title — "CALL" or "QUOTE" with an icon identifying the button type.Active/Inactive toggle — Enables or disables the button on your live website in real time. When toggled off, visitors will not see that button.Edit — Opens the edit form to change the button's text and destination URLs.Button text preview — Shows the current English and French labels side by side (e.g., "Free consultation" / "Consultation gratuite" for CALL, "Free quote" / "Devis gratuit" for QUOTE).URLs — The destination links for each language. CALL links to a Cal.com booking page (https://cal.memopyk.com/...). QUOTE links to a Zoho Forms quote request (https://zfrmz.eu/...).Active/Inactive badge — Green "Active" when the button is live on the site, grey "Inactive" when hidden.✏️ Edit FormClick Edit on a card to open the edit form below:English Button Text — The label visitors see in English (e.g., "Free consultation").French Button Text — The label visitors see in French (e.g., "Consultation gratuite").English URL — Where English visitors go when they click. Use a full URL: a Cal.com booking link (https://cal.memopyk.com/#/memopykl), a Zoho form (https://zfrmz.eu/...), or any web page.French URL — Where French visitors go. Can point to a French variant of the same service or a different page entirely.Active — Toggle to enable or disable this button.Save Changes — Saves your edits. Changes appear on the live site immediately.Cancel — Closes the form without saving.💡 TipsKeep button text short and action-oriented — "Free consultation" works better than "Click here to schedule an appointment with our team."After changing a URL, visit your site and click the button to verify it leads to the correct booking or form page.Disable a button temporarily with the toggle to hide it without losing its settings — useful during seasonal campaigns or maintenance.Both buttons appear site-wide, so any change takes effect on every page immediately.How do I...Create a blog postStep-by-step guide to create a blog post, manually or with AI assistanceTranslate a postTranslate a post to another language using AI or manual toolsNeed more help? helpText:
HelpThis Screen
  AI Context — Brand Brain for Claude

  The AI Context (Brand Brain) defines how Claude writes for MEMOPYK. Every AI-generated blog post, translation, and content piece uses these guidelines automatically. Think of it as training Claude to write in MEMOPYK's voice.

  What You See
  Six entries grouped into two categories:
  
    Brand Guidelines — Voice, tone, product terminology, target audience, and messaging rules.
    Translation Rules — How to translate French and English while preserving MEMOPYK's brand identity.
  

  Entry Cards
  Each card shows:
  
    Title — What this guideline covers (e.g., Brand Voice and Tone).
    Key — Internal identifier (e.g., brand_voice).
    Updated timestamp — When this entry was last modified and by whom.
    Content preview — The full guideline text in a gray code block.
    Edit button (top-right of each card) — Opens the editor to modify this guideline.
  

  Editing Guidelines
  Click Edit on any entry to open the editor:
  
    Modify the content in the large text area (supports markdown-style formatting).
    Click Save (orange button) to commit changes.
    Click Cancel to discard changes.
  
  All future AI content generation will use the updated guidelines immediately.

  Where This Context Is Used
  
    Blog post generation — When you click Create Post in Planned Posts, Claude uses these guidelines to write the article.
    AI translations — French and English translations follow the translation rules entry.
    Content suggestions — When Claude suggests image concepts, internal links, or meta descriptions, it uses the brand guidelines.
  

  Quick Tips
  
    Keep guidelines concise but specific. Avoid jargon is vague. Use film souvenir not memory video is actionable.
    Update the target audience entry when your market strategy changes (e.g., expanding to Canadian French market).
    The translation rules entry is critical for maintaining consistent French terminology across all bilingual content.
    If Claude starts generating off-brand content, check the Brand Voice and Tone entry first — it is the most influential guideline.
    The info card at the bottom of the page shows a link to the full context view. This is for reference only — all content generation uses these guidelines automatically.
